# Do unobserved practice counters improve recall forecasts?

The released counts are available before each practice. For recurrent learner–lexeme pairs, compare those counts with what the previous recorded encounter would imply if the trace were complete. The differences can reflect missing encounters, grouping errors, or inconsistent clocks. We do not label them as known extra practice. Compare these differences with a matched tree that sees all primitive previous counters and timestamps and the same learner ability residuals. Also test trees with only the former history features, registered frozen CPU history CatBoost, previous counters alone, residuals alone and an item-rate rule. All use the same published sessions, language-qualified lexeme keys and learner weighting at evaluation.

Reuse the learner hash buckets 10–11 for training, 12 for calibration and 13 for screening. Train equal-row-weight fractional CrossEntropy GPU CatBoost with depth 6, 500 iterations, seed 42, learning rate .05. The historical CPU comparator retains its own previously selected configuration. Calibrate positive logit slope and intercept on calibration learners, evaluating both identity and calibrated probabilities there and retaining the lower calibration loss for each newly fitted model. For preexisting CPU predictions retain the frozen calibration. Measure average session log loss within each learner then mean across learners. Screen at .005 nats against every control. Report simultaneous paired learner intervals with Bonferroni t endpoints. Development evidence supports method selection only.

Availability is strictly before the current practice timestamp. Pool simultaneous learner–item rows, sum their observed successes/exposures and use previous counters only if that earlier block agrees on their values. Prior learner ability uses mean earlier residuals relative to a training-only cross-fitted lexeme difficulty estimate. A second estimator averages earlier residuals within learner and part of speech. Held-out learners and all their practice outcomes are absent from the difficulty lookup. Source targets never serve as own-row predictors. Keep other hash buckets excluded from all study computations.
